messages.content: Predict this participant's actual cash contribution in a one-time community matching-funds game in Lofa County, Liberia. Twenty-four adults from different households are selected. Each receives three 100-Liberian-dollar notes, totaling 300 LD. The nominal instructions are to put 0, 1, 2 or 3 of those notes into a private envelope for a community development fund and keep the un-contributed notes. The announced allocation plan assigns half the selected players a contribution multiplier of 2 and half a multiplier of 5; each person is told their own multiplier before choosing. The multiplier applies to the total amount credited to the community fund: a 100-LD contribution becomes 200 LD at multiplier 2, or 500 LD at multiplier 5. It is not an additional 200 or 500 LD on top of the contribution. Funds go to three community representatives to implement community-selected development projects, not to an equal cash division among the 24 players. Both women and men may benefit from projects regardless of the selected players' gender composition. A community meeting explaining the opportunity took place about a week before game day, leaving time for local mobilization; your personal attendance, contacts, project knowledge and private expectations are not supplied unless reliably established. Your envelope choice is private; you are not shown other participants' current contributions or the final fund total before choosing. There is no prior round of this game in the supplied record. Earlier public community reconstruction support is background context, not an instruction about how to act. The participant attributes supplied are factual self-reports about pre-existing characteristics; unavailable or inconsistent attributes are omitted. The prediction target is the actual amount placed in the envelope, not a recommendation or a test of rule compliance. Output only that amount as a nonnegative integer in Liberian dollars, without explanation; do not turn it into a note count, round it to a prescribed category, or clip it to the initial allocation.
